summary: Remote shell backdoor via hardcoded WebRTC signaling relay
details: The package's `vanexa-agent` bin launches a daemon that establishes a WebRTC session against a hardcoded signaling relay at https://vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev and exposes a `terminal.exec` tool wired to `spawn('/bin/bash', ['-c', <command>])` on Linux/macOS and `cmd.exe /c <command>` on Windows. Commands delivered over the WebRTC DataChannel from the paired remote party are executed as shell on the host running the daemon, providing arbitrary remote code execution. The daemon supports a fully-autonomous mode without per-command approval. The signaling host (`tubefood.workers.dev`) is a Cloudflare Workers subdomain not brand-matched to the package's `vanexa` identity. The primary runtime is shipped as V8 bytecode (`dist/bundle.jsc`, loaded via `bytenode`) with a `dist/bundle.cjs` fallback, reducing transparency of the executed logic.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
